label: Accordion
title: Accordion
summary: Reveal supporting details when people need them, while keeping the page easy to scan.
corePrinciple: Make the header a clear promise about the content inside.

anatomy.title: A heading opens onto supporting content
anatomy.description: The header makes a clear promise, the indicator shows whether it is open, and the content slot reveals supporting detail when people ask for it.
blocks: The title is the promise people use to decide whether to open the section.
Keep the header short enough to remain scannable in a narrow host.
The public component switches between add and minus icons as it opens and closes.
The component’s bottom border separates the open section from the following content.
Put supporting details or related public rows here; keep primary actions visible in the page flow.

configuration.title: Choose the surface treatment deliberately
configuration.description: The default treatment is quiet until interaction. Contained keeps the filled header treatment visible so a grouped section can stand apart from its host.
blocks: Let the page carry the surface
Use the default when the heading can sit comfortably in the surrounding page structure.
Use contained when the filled header should keep related supporting content together.

states.description: Expanded, disabled, and hover feedback come from the public component as people interact. Configure the values that describe the product situation and let the runtime derive the visual state.

sizing.title: Give the host room to tell the story
sizing.description: The Figma reference is 445px wide. In a product layout, the host supplies width and the component grows with its title and open content.
blocks: Keep the title and content on one clear line when the host has space.
Allow a long title to wrap when the group name needs more than one line.

content.title: Use the slot for supporting detail
content.description: The header should tell people what they will find. The open content can add context, related rows, or secondary explanations without hiding the page’s primary task.
blocks: Use a meaningful header and let the body answer the question that header raises.
Rows or short explanatory text belong in the content slot when they answer the header’s promise.
Leave the main task in the page flow when hiding it would block progress or change the decision.

doDont.title: Make the hidden detail worth opening
doDont.description: Clear promises, related content, and visible primary work help a disclosure stay useful without becoming a hiding place.
blocks: A specific promise lets people decide whether opening the section is useful.
Use a heading with no meaning
People must open the section before they know whether it contains the detail they need.

The heading stops helping because the open content answers several different questions.
Use the Accordion for supporting details while the main payment action stays in the page flow.
Hide the primary action in the body
The button is unavailable until someone expands the section, so the task is harder to complete.

sources.title: Grounded in the published component
sources.description: This guide records the public Accordion contract, the inspected Figma source, and the published story configurations used by the examples.
blocks: Default, contained, expanded, disabled, list, and group examples

Examples use public Accordion, ListItem, IconCapsule, MoneyValue, and Text exports from jfs-components 0.1.60. The package registry latest is also 0.1.60. The Accordion derives its state from public props and pointer interaction; the guide does not pass the internal Accordion States mode. The Figma reference includes a 445px header and content-driven open example, while package height follows its children and token padding. React Native Web can apply the package's requested LayoutAnimation immediately; the guide leaves that shipped behavior unchanged.
